title: All Paths All at Once: A Quantum Monte Carlo and Neural Committor Approach to Reaction Pathway Search
abstract: arXiv:2611.03699v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Locating competing reaction pathways is difficult when potential-energy gradients are unavailable. Here we present tReax_expedition, an energy-only approach combining coupled Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labelling and restrained continuation. Exploration identifies connected states, while continuation resolves candidate channels and records sampled chain maxima. Single-search benchmarks on three two-dimensional potentials recovered an intermediate and competing routes without transition-state guesses. For eight of nine gas-phase reactions on GFN2-xTB, sampled chain maxima differed from independently refined saddle energies by less than 0.76 kJ/mol. Alanine dipeptide instead revealed incomplete conformational relaxation, showing that route connectivity can persist despite structural and energetic errors. Neural committor learning and local straddling-pair sampling connect the resulting paths to transition-region sa

translated_title: 所有路径一次获取：一种结合量子蒙特卡洛与神经commitor的反应路径搜索方法
translated_abstract: 在势能梯度不可用时，寻找相互竞争的反应路径十分困难。本文提出tReax_expedition，一种仅依赖能量信息的方法，它将耦合蒙特卡洛探索、随机淬火标记与受限延续相结合。探索阶段识别相互连通的状态，而延续阶段解析候选反应通道并记录采样链的最大值。在三个二维势能面上的单次搜索基准测试中，该方法在无需过渡态猜测的情况下成功恢复出中间体和相互竞争的反应路线。在基于GFN2-xTB势能面的九个气相反应中，有八个反应的采样链最大值与独立精修后的鞍点能量之差小于0.76 kJ/mol。而丙氨酸二肽的算例则揭示了构象弛豫不完全的问题，表明尽管存在结构和能量上的误差，反应路径的连通性仍可保持。通过神经commitor学习和局域跨对采样，所得反应路径可与过渡区域样本相连（原文此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出一种无需势能梯度的仅能量反应路径搜索方法tReax_expedition，通过耦合蒙特卡洛探索、随机淬火标记与受限延续自动恢复中间体和竞争反应通道，无需过渡态猜测即可将链最大值能量精确到精修鞍点0.76 kJ/mol以内，并借助神经commitor学习将路径与过渡区域采样相连接。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces tReax_expedition, a gradient-free, energy-only reaction pathway search method combining coupled Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labeling, and restrained continuation, which recovers intermediates and competing routes without transition-state guesses—with sampled chain maxima within 0.76 kJ/mol of refined saddle energies—and further links the resulting paths to transition-region samples via neural committor learning.
